Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 July,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:14749
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Ashish Shroti
 On The 16th Of July, 2025
 Writ Petition No. 19351 of 2022
 Dayal Singh Parihar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Mr. Santosh Kumar Agrawal - Advocate for the petition
 Mr. Brij Mohan Patel - Ga for the State.
 Order

The petitioner has filed this writ petition challenging the order, dated 26.07.2022, (Annexure P-1)
whereby punishment of recovery of Rs.4,82,423/- has been imposed upon the petitioner.
He has been also imposed with the punishment of censure.
2. The petitioner, during the period from 29.09.2015 to 30.11.2020, was posted as Range Assistant in Seondha Range, Forest Division, Datia.

In relation to certain illegal excavation of the minerals, a charge-sheet under Rule 16 of The Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Classification, Control & Appeal)
Rules, 1966 was issued to the petitioner on 28.11.2020 (Annexure P-3).

sentences.text:
The petitioner gave detailed reply to this charge-sheet on 21.10.2021 (Annexure P-4) and, thereafter, the respondents have passed the impugned order on 25.07.2022, whereby the petitioner was found guilty of dereliction of duty, as a result of which loss of Rs.4,82,423/- was caused to the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:14749 2 WP-19351-2022 Government, which has been directed to be recovered from the petitioner.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner challenged the impugned order of punishment on two grounds.

Firstly, he submitted that since the petitioner raised disputed question of facts in his reply,
a detailed departmental enquiry ought to have been conducted by the respondents under Rule 14 of CCA Rules.
Secondly, he submitted that since the petitioner had already retired on 30.09.2020, the punishment order could not have been passed without the approval of the Governor.
The learned counsel for the petitioner also challenged the finding recorded against him in the impugned order on merits.
He, therefore, prays for setting aside the impugned order.

Counsel for the petitioner placed reliance upon the Apex Court judgment in the case of O.K. Bharadwaj Vs. Union of India &

On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents supported the impugned order and submitted that admittedly during the period from 29.09.2015 to 30.11.2020, the petitioner was posted as Range Assistant in Seondha Range, Forest Division, Datia, wherein illegal excavation of minerals were found.

He further submitted that the petitioner has not disputed the fact that he was responsible for the safety and security of the forest range and, therefore, since the loss is caused to the Government during the period of his posting, he has been rightly imposed with the punishment of recovery of the amount to the loss caused to the Government.
He further submits that the respondent Divisional Forest Officer was competent to impose punishment upon the petitioner.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14749 3 WP-19351-2022 5.
Considered the arguments and perused the record.
6. Firstly, the ground raised by the counsel for the petitioner with regard to the conduct of the detailed enquiry under Rule 14 of CCA Rules needs to be considered.
Learned counsel for the petitioner in support of his submission has placed reliance upon the judgment of Apex Court in the case o f O.K. Bharadwaj (supra).
However, the judgment passed in the said case was considered and explained by this Court in the case of Roop Singh Bhadouria Vs. State of M.P. & others (W.P.No.7788/2011) .

entities.text: Roop Singh Bhadouria Vs. State of M.P. & others (W.P.No.7788/2011)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After considering various judgments including the judgment of O.K.
Bharadwaj (Supra), this Court held that while imposing minor punishment, a detailed enquiry is not required to be conducted in every case.

This Court has held in para 17 & 18 as under :
"17.
Division Bench of this Court in the case of Ratan Singh Silawat (supra) has held in similar lines as held in the case of C.P. Singh (supra).

Learned Division Bench after considering all judgments in instant realm concluded that it is the discretion of departmental authority in such cases where Minor Punishment is intended to be inflicted whether to hold departmental inquiry or not.

It differs from case to case,
therefore, it is not automatic.
Otherwise provision of summary procedure would lose its meaning.

18. Therefore, it is a discretion of the authority in the given fact situation whether in a case of minor penalty when employee denies the charges, then departmental inquiry is required to be held or not.

Holding of departmental inquiry is not automatic and not in every case of minor penalty departmental inquiry is required to be conducted as per the Rule 16 of the Rules, 1966, as per the mandate of Apex Court in the case of FCI (supra) and later on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:14749 4 WP-19351-2022 interpreted by the Division Bench of this Court in the matter of C.P.
Singh (supra).

However, said discretion is to be exercised reasonably and objectively and it should not be guided by the arbitrariness."
7.
Considering the aforesaid legal position, if the facts of the present case are seen, the authorities have given detailed reasons while recording the finding against the petitioner.

It has been found that Dayal Singh Parihar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30314626/
2 the petitioner was posted in the Forest Range Seondha during the period from 29.05.2019 to 30.11.2020, during which period about 10 pits were found, which were about 7-8 months old.

sentences.text: Again during the inspection on 20.02.2020 and 21.02.2020, 11 pits about one year old were found in the same compartment.
The findings have been recorded after giving opportunity to the petitioner and supported by GPS mapping, also with panchanama prepared in presence of independent persons.
Since the petitioner was posted in the Forest Range during the aforesaid period, he is rightly been found responsible for illegal excavation.

The total loss was calculated to be Rs.14,13,505/- and the petitioner has been found liable to pay the amount to the extend of 30 % of the total amount i.e.
Rs.4,82,423/-.
Thus, it cannot be said that finding recorded by the authorities are perverse or without any justification.
8. The learned counsel for the petitioner tried to assail the finding recorded by the authority on merits of the case.
However, the petitioner has chosen not to file departmental appeal against the impugned order, where he could have challenged the finding on merits also.
Before this Court, he can only succeed if can show defect in decision making process of passing the impugned order.

Thus, it is found that the process adopted by the respondents NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:14749 5 WP-19351-2022 in imposing punishment is in consonance with Rule 16 of CCA Rules.
9.
In view of discussion made above, the petition is found to be without any substance and is accordingly dismissed.

(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE bj/-
